Ephemeral means lasting for a very short time. Think of soap bubbles popping moments after they form, or how morning dew disappears by noon — gone before you've barely noticed. It's useful because it gives you a single word for anything that's brief and fleeting, from social media posts to a mayfly's lifespan. Source: dictionary definition.

Ephemeral means lasting only a short time — fleeting or temporary. Think of a mayfly, which lives for about a day, or a text message that disappears after being read. It's a useful word for describing anything that's fleeting and gone before you know it, from summer blooms to trendy internet memes. Source: Wikipedia article on ephemerality.

The Eiffel Tower is a wrought-iron lattice tower on the Champ de Mars in Paris, France. Built from 1887 to 1889, it was designed by the engineering firm of Gustave Eiffel, for whom it's named. It was originally constructed as the entrance arch for the 1889 World's Fair and has since become one of the most recognizable landmarks in the world.

The Eiffel Tower is an iconic iron lattice tower on the Champ de Mars in Paris, France. Built from 1887 to 1889 for the World's Fair, it's named after engineer Gustave Eiffel, whose company designed and constructed it. Standing 330 meters (1,083 ft) tall, it was the tallest man-made structure in the world until 1930 and remains one of the most-visited paid monuments globally.

The Eiffel Tower is a wrought-iron lattice tower on the Champ de Mars in Paris, France, named after engineer Gustave Eiffel, whose firm designed and built it from 1887 to 1889. Originally constructed as the centerpiece for the 1889 World's Fair, it was built to celebrate the centennial of the French Revolution. Standing 330 meters (1,083 ft) tall, it was the world's tallest man-made structure for 41 years and remains one of the most-visited paid monuments in the world.
